events.title: Gold Discovered at Sutter's Mill
events.description: James W. Marshall found gold flakes in the American River at Sutter's Mill in Coloma, California, while overseeing construction of a sawmill for John Sutter.
events.significance: The discovery triggered the California Gold Rush of 1849, drawing roughly 300,000 people to California, accelerating its path to statehood in 1850 and reshaping the economy and demographics of the American West.

events.title: First Canned Beer Sold
events.description: The Gottfried Krueger Brewing Company of Newark, New Jersey, began selling Krueger's Finest Beer and Cream Ale in cans to customers in Richmond, Virginia, after a successful test market.
events.significance: Canned beer proved popular and practical, helping transform the beverage packaging industry and consumer habits after the end of Prohibition.

events.title: Death of Winston Churchill
events.description: Sir Winston Churchill, the British statesman who led the United Kingdom through World War II as Prime Minister, died at age 90 in London, 70 years to the day after his father Lord Randolph Churchill's death.
events.significance: Churchill's death prompted a state funeral on a scale not seen for a non-royal in Britain, and marked the passing of one of the 20th century's most influential leaders, remembered for his wartime oratory and resolve.

events.title: Apple Macintosh Introduced
events.description: Apple Computer unveiled the Macintosh personal computer, announced by Steve Jobs at the company's shareholder meeting in Cupertino, following the famous '1984' Super Bowl commercial days later.
events.significance: The Macintosh popularized the graphical user interface and mouse for mainstream consumers, shaping the future of personal computing and desktop publishing.

events.title: Shoichi Yokoi Found in Guam
events.description: Japanese soldier Shoichi Yokoi was discovered living in the jungles of Guam, where he had hidden for nearly 28 years after the island's liberation in 1944, unaware that World War II had ended.
events.significance: His discovery drew worldwide attention to the phenomenon of Japanese holdouts and the enduring influence of wartime loyalty, and his return to Japan sparked national debate.
